steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react' here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building a React component with state.
successCriteria: The code must include an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the import statement needs to include both React and useState from 'react'. Check the syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. The component should be defined below the imports.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure it returns something (like a div) to satisfy JSX requirements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App is created with a return statement that outputs JSX.
successCriteria: The code includes a component named App that returns valid JSX (e.g., a div with some content).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This is the foundation of your React application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns JSX (like a div or other React element).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'App' and included a return statement with JSX.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called isAuthenticated with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Remember to use TypeScript generics with useState to specify the type as boolean.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your App component will have an isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false, ready to track authentication status.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call with the variable name 'isAuthenticated', type annotation '<boolean>', and initial value 'false'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the authentication state. The isAuthenticated variable will track whether the user is logged in.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) Used the exact variable name 'isAuthenticated', 2) Added the type '<boolean>', and 3) Set the initial value to 'false'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the App component, use useState to create a boolean state variable called isAuthenticated starting as false.

steps.title: Initialize user info state
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, use useState to create a state variable named 'user' with an initial value of null. This will store user information when authenticated.
steps.hint: Add a second useState call after your existing isAuthenticated state. Remember to import useState from 'react' if not already imported.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a user state
const [user, setUser] = useState<{name: string} | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has two state variables: isAuthenticated (boolean) and user (null initially).
successCriteria: useState
user
setUser
null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the user state with useState. This will allow us to store user information when authentication happens.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly declared the user state with useState. Check that you have: 1) Used useState, 2) Named the variable 'user', 3) Set the initial value to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on just initializing the user state. You need to add a second useState call inside the App component to create a 'user' state variable initialized to null.

steps.title: Define login handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleLogin inside your App component. This function should set isAuthenticated to true when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsAuthenticated with true. You can define it as an arrow function or a regular function.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleLogin function that sets the authentication state to true.
successCriteria: The handleLogin function must be defined inside the App component and must call setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the login handler function that will update the authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named handleLogin and it calls setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogin function is not properly defined. It should be inside the App component and update isAuthenticated to true.

steps.title: Define logout handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleLogout inside your App component. This function should set isAuthenticated to false and clear the user state by setting it to null.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsAuthenticated(false) and setUser(null).
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogout function is defined that updates both authentication and user states.
successCriteria: The handleLogout function should be defined with the correct name, call setIsAuthenticated(false), and call setUser(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the logout handler function that will clear authentication and user data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleLogout function sets isAuthenticated to false and clears the user state by setting it to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Define a function named handleLogout that calls setIsAuthenticated(false) and setUser(null).

steps.title: Add user info display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element that conditionally displays the user's name when authenticated. Use the existing `user` state variable and `isAuthenticated` state to control the display.
steps.hint:
Use a ternary operator or logical AND operator to conditionally render a

element containing the user's name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display the user's name when authenticated, and show nothing when not authenticated.
successCriteria: Add a paragraph element that conditionally renders based on `isAuthenticated` state and displays the `user` value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the user information. The paragraph will only appear when the user is authenticated.

steps.title: Add login button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main container with the text 'Login' and wire its onClick event to call the handleLogin function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with onClick={handleLogin} and the text content 'Login'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with 'Login' text appears in the UI that, when clicked, will trigger the handleLogin function.
successCriteria: The code includes a <button> element with onClick={handleLogin} and the text content 'Login'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a login button with the correct click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button has both the correct onClick handler and the text 'Login'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct onClick handler or text. Try adding <button onClick={handleLogin}>Login</button>.

steps.title: Add logout button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Define the handleLogout function inside your component. It should set isAuthenticated to false and user to null.
steps.hint: Create a function called handleLogout that calls setIsAuthenticated(false) and setUser(null).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a complete handleLogout function that properly updates both authentication states.
successCriteria: The handleLogout function should be defined with the correct name, call setIsAuthenticated(false) and setUser(null), and have a void return type annotation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleLogout function that will reset authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleLogout function calls both setIsAuthenticated(false) and setUser(null).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogout function isn't defined correctly. It should update both state variables to reset authentication.
